# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s148) | **#897 MERGED — develop `400517aaf`, the deploy blocker closed on the trunk, with a negative control PROVED to discriminate in BOTH directions** (2026-09-07 22:24) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **Tree predicted BEFORE the merge by two methods that agreed in advance** (`2be0aaa8…`), re-derived from the commit object after; parents `6a7a7824e` + `48c4d8053`. **Positive controls:** the non-exhaustive 403 text 0 before / 1 after, corrected runtime message travelled. **THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS THE KEEPER — it shows it can answer BOTH ways before it is believed:** #892's three test files absent from develop (0), **plus a file that IS there (`slot_target.test.sh` = 1)** and **the same files present on #892 (1)**. Its line: *"a zero that cannot distinguish 'not merged' from 'the query is broken' is not a control — and tonight I hit four separate checks that could not fail."* **KS-978 → Tested Not Deployed, NOT Done, because it is a deploy blocker and nothing shipped** — carrying the receipt, the published wording, and the scenario-H limit **verbatim**. **Pushed the KS-811 justification up rather than letting it go quiet:** *"without the derived comparison, the next contract author is in the same position the last one was."* **Collected its own four could-not-fail checks in ONE place rather than scattered** — three zsh `nomatch` kills that read as zero hits, and a `$M:path` expansion. |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s148) | **Amended #897 to close both findings in one edit — and caught a weakening its OWN amendment introduced that no suite and no re-gate could have found** (2026-09-07 22:20) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | `718008cef` → `48c4d8053`. **F-1:** list now explicitly non-exhaustive, points at `error.code`, and names what it MEASURED — the route guard, `documents:write`, `onBehalfOf`, organizationUuid and the four gateway codes. **F-2 fixed in THREE places** (field description, 403 description, **and the runtime message**) *because two would not have worked* — and that forced a **fourth** edit it flagged: the KS-597 bind cell asserted on that message, so changing it alone would have reddened a cell **for the right reason** and invited a revert. **🔴 THE KEEPER:** adding the `onBehalfOf` clause made the existing cell's `/different Organisation/i` match **that** clause instead of the subject — **still green, no longer pinning what it named.** Tightened to `/DIFFERS FROM/` and added three cells; 7 → 10. Its own line: *"the second time tonight a change of mine made a green cell stop testing what it claimed — a quieter failure than a red one."* **Only the author re-reading could find that; a re-gate could not.** **STRUCTURAL INSIGHT, better than the defect:** the four gateway codes have **zero** hits in `services/originate` — they live in `api-gateway/.../enforcement.ts`, so *"a contract author reading only the service that owns the route cannot see them"* — which explains recurrence rather than blame and justifies KS-811's derived comparison. Red-proof 3/10, all three the 403 cells, **10 executed**, restored byte-identical. Scenario-H limit put ON KS-978, not left in a mail. |

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.
